chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who carried provisions on his head, and they struck a person so he died, or something broke from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is responsible (liable for compensation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability for accidental injury caused by carrying items on one's head?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *daman* (liability) for accidental injury caused by carrying goods on one's head, a specific application of the broader legal maxim regarding 'substantial causes' (*sabab*). It clarifies that the carrier bears financial responsibility (*diya*) regardless of whether the outcome is death or physical fracture, reflecting the Imami juristic view on direct causation in tort law. This ruling is often cited alongside the well-digging precedent to illustrate how liability attaches to the actor's control over the hazardous object.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirhan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who carried provisions upon his head, so they struck a human being and he died, or something broke from him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is responsible’.
